title: Hello, Next.js: Why We Are Migrating
summary: The reasons behind moving our publishing platform from a custom PHP stack to Next.js.
body:
Our PHP platform has served us well for over a decade.

But shipping new experiences has become slow. Next.js gives us server rendering, a modern component model and first-class TypeScript.

This article kicks off a series documenting the migration.
author: Jane Doe

headline: Five TypeScript Tips for Former C# Developers
body:
If you know C#, TypeScript will feel familiar.

Prefer union types over enums, lean on type inference, and enable strict mode from day one.

title: Legacy PHP Patterns We Are Leaving Behind
content:
Global state, mixed HTML and SQL, and include-driven routing.

Each pattern made sense once. Today they slow us down.

title: Migrating Page by Page Without Downtime
body:
The strangler fig pattern lets new and old systems run side by side.

Requests for migrated pages go to the new app; everything else still reaches the legacy system.
author: John Smith

headline: Caching Strategies for Content Sites
body:
Content changes rarely but is read constantly.

Time-based revalidation keeps pages fast while still picking up edits within a minute.
